note: The original description by Emerson 1925 (new species), with only the soldier and the alate nymph, no worker recorded. The text was extracted by OCR from the library scan on Internet Archive, and a few figures may be affected by recognition.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head dark reddish brown, broad, spherical; outline fairly straight or slightly concave, with a swelling at the base of the nasus; hairy (with shorter hairs than in Armitermes acajutlae), with longer setae visible — 4 at the base of the nasus and 4 on the vertex. Antennae yellow except near the base, 14-segmented, segment 3 shorter than segment 2, segment 2 about as long as segment 4. Nasus about the same colour as the rest of the head, of moderate length and thickness, hairless except at the apex. Pronotum dark brown, the anterior margin with long setae and short hairs, slightly concave. Legs yellowish brown. Abdominal tergites dark brown, densely hairy, with a row of setae at the margins; sternites paler. Measurements: body length 4.00—5.00 mm; head length 1.64—1.80 mm; head width 1.16—1.25 mm; antennal length 1.93 mm; pronotum width 0.55—0.61 mm; hind tibia length 1.28—1.32 mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: (Winged nymph) antennae 15-segmented. Compound eyes not very large. Ocelli rather far from the compound eyes. Posterior margin of the pronotum distinctly concave.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Compared with N. pilifrons (Holmgren): the latter has a paler abdomen, 13-segmented antennae and is smaller on average; compared with N. arenarius (Bates): the latter has less hair on the head; compared with N. acajutlae (Holmgren): the latter has yellow abdominal tergites and a few hairs on the nasus. Type locality: Kartabo, British Guiana; known only from the type locality. The description is based on numerous soldiers and alate nymphs collected by the author in the same queenless colony; the type specimen is a soldier.
